tier_reason: First-party primes timings in the README (repeated in docs/performance.md) with benchmark code public at commit 9481d653 (benchmarks/primes.py, primes.lua, primes.cpp, all of which assert the expected result) and the CPU stated (i5-12400F, WSL Ubuntu 20.04), but no compiler or build flags for pkpy, CPython or Lua, so not A; no independent measurement, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Primes benchmark: pkpy 1.2.7 2.385 s vs CPython 3.8.10 2.871 s (about 1.2x, derived from page data); Lua 5.3.3 took 1.576 s (about 1.5x faster than pkpy, derived from page data) and C++ (gnu++11) 0.104 s. The README also says 'Currently, pkpy is as fast as cpython 3.9', but docs/performance.md calls the 1.2.7 numbers historical and says to use them 'as historical observations, not as a claim of equivalence to a particular CPython release'.
corrections.caveats: Does not beat the category's in-list baseline: in its own table Lua 5.3.3 is about 1.5x faster than pkpy. The win over CPython is small (about 1.2x), on one benchmark, against an old CPython 3.8.10, and was measured on pkpy 1.2.7; the project's docs/performance.md says these 1.2.7 results 'are not a benchmark of the current 2.x C11 interpreter'. Compiler and flags not stated for any of the measured builds. The linked performance page (pocketpy.github.io/performance) and an older 1.2.6 CI comparison were not opened. Listed to document the shortcoming.

notes: Numbers, versions and hardware match the README exactly; the primes scripts at the recorded commit are equivalent across languages and check their output, so the evidence is valid but thin and dated. Shortcomings to record: slower than Lua (in-list baseline) by about 1.5x; only a 1.2x win over CPython 3.8 on one script; numbers predate the 2.x C11 rewrite and the project itself disclaims them; no compiler/flags. CPython is an in-list baseline for language-interpreters, not for embedded-scripting.

tier_reason: Upgraded from C: the yk team's public benchmark harness (ykjit/yk-benchmarks rebench.conf, common.sh, suites/awfy, suites/cbgame, suites/realworld, suites/yk) runs yklua against stock PUC Lua 5.5.0, the build flags are in common.sh and yklua's src/Makefile, and each published results file records the CPU (AMD EPYC 7F52); the gh-pages summary gives a geomean time ratio of 0.513. Only the gcc version is unpinned.

corrections.baseline: PUC-Rio Lua 5.5.0 (stock lua.org tarball, the version yklua is based on) built with -flto as an LTO baseline
corrections.claimed_speedup: Geometric mean execution-time ratio yklua/Lua of 0.513 (about 1.95x faster) over 22 benchmarks in the 2026-10-06 11:14 nightly run (index lists 0.504 to 0.519 for the last 10 runs). Per-benchmark mean iteration times from that run's data file (derived from page data): Mandelbrot(500) 370.2 ms vs 63.4 ms (5.84x), BigLoop 3.90x, spectralnorm 3.30x, Heightmap 3.18x, Sieve 3.01x, NBody 2.88x, fannkuchredux 2.33x, Queens 2.15x, Permute 2.08x, Bounce 1.99x, Towers 1.81x, LuLPeg 1.71x, Richards 1.59x, Json 1.52x, knucleotide 1.47x, List 1.37x, CD 1.36x, HashIds 1.35x, binarytrees 1.33x, Storage 1.23x, DeltaBlue 1.11x, Havlak 1.09x; geomean without the in-house BigLoop loop about 1.89x (derived from page data). Laurence Tratt's 2026 blog post reports 'a geometric mean speedup of a little under 2x' with about 400 lines added and under 50 changed in PUC Lua (snippet only); the Mandelbrot 3.2 s to 0.8 s figure in the original record was not found on any page opened.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Baseline: Lua 5.5.0 stock Makefile (gcc -std=gnu99, -O2 in yklua's copy of the same Makefile) with MYCFLAGS=-flto; yklua: ykllvm (yk's LLVM/clang fork) via yk-config release --cflags --cppflags, -O2, -DUSE_YK -DLUA_USE_JUMPTABLE=0 (ykjit/yk-benchmarks common.sh, ykjit/yklua src/Makefile). gcc version not stated.
corrections.hardware: AMD EPYC 7F52 16-Core Processor (host bencher14), Debian kernel 6.12.57, recorded in the rebench results file
corrections.workload: ykjit/yk-benchmarks nightly ReBench suite: 14 Are-We-Fast-Yet Lua benchmarks, 4 Computer Language Benchmarks Game programs (fannkuchredux, spectralnorm, knucleotide, binarytrees), 3 real-world programs (LuLPeg, HashIds, Heightmap) and the in-house BigLoop; 5 process invocations x 10 in-process iterations each, yklua vs stock Lua 5.5.0.
corrections.license: MIT (PUC-Rio Lua notice in src/lua.h and doc/readme.html); no repository-level LICENSE file covering the Yk additions
corrections.caveats: Experimental (README says so) and not drop-in: building needs the yk toolchain (Rust nightly, ykllvm, yk-config). Means include JIT warm-up iterations; gains are uneven (DeltaBlue 1.11x, Havlak 1.09x, Storage 1.23x) and the 5.84x Mandelbrot and 3.90x BigLoop results are loop-heavy microbenchmarks. Baseline and yklua are built by different compilers (gcc -O2 -flto vs ykllvm clang), and yklua disables Lua's jump-table dispatch. Results come from a rolling nightly snapshot on the gh-pages branch (force-pushed each run), so the cited data file may be replaced. Blog figures (under 2x geomean, about 400 lines added, does not reach LuaJIT's peak performance) are snippet only since tratt.net and infoq.com are blocked. No LICENSE file at the repo root: the Lua core carries PUC-Rio's MIT notice but the Yk-specific changes have no stated licence.

notes: Found the real numbers page: ykjit/yk-benchmarks publishes nightly ReBench results (geomean 0.513 time ratio, about 1.95x over 22 benchmarks) with the harness, build script and CPU all public, so this is a reproducible A-tier comparison against stock PUC Lua 5.5.0. The record's Mandelbrot 3.2 s to 0.8 s figure was not found and is replaced by per-benchmark ratios from the data file. Shortcomings: experimental, needs the yk toolchain, uneven gains (1.09x to 5.84x), different compilers for baseline and yklua, no repo licence for the Yk additions (usability mixed), 7 stars.

tier_reason: Upgraded from C: the repo's statistics/times-slow.txt holds 20 timed runs per benchmark of LuaAOT, the stock Lua 5.4.3 interpreter and LuaJIT (experiments/*.lua, scripts/compile with gcc -O2 -g), and the peer-reviewed SBLP 2021 paper 'A Surprisingly Simple Lua Compiler' (Gualandi and Ierusalimschy; extended version in Journal of Computer Languages 2022) reports a 20% to 60% running-time reduction (abstract seen as search snippet only). Not A: no CPU model or gcc version in the repo, and the paper could not be opened.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'For numerical benchmarks it can be twice as fast as regular Lua. But overall, it is not as fast as LuaJIT or Pallene.' Repo statistics/times-slow.txt (mean wall time of 20 runs, LuaAOT vs Lua 5.4.3 interpreter, derived from page data): binarytrees 2.68 s vs 3.51 s (1.31x), fannkuch 21.92 vs 44.31 s (2.02x), fasta 3.84 vs 5.05 s (1.32x), knucleotide 3.44 vs 4.15 s (1.21x), mandelbrot 6.17 vs 16.27 s (2.64x), nbody 12.14 vs 18.23 s (1.50x), spectralnorm 19.00 vs 39.86 s (2.10x). LuaJIT on the same runs was 2.4x to 31x faster than Lua. SBLP 2021 paper abstract: LuaAOT reduced benchmark running times by 20% to 60% (snippet only).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Interpreter built with the Lua 5.4.3 Makefile (gcc -std=gnu99 -O2, make guess); benchmark modules compiled with gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -g (scripts/compile). gcc version not stated.
corrections.workload: Seven Computer Language Benchmarks Game programs in experiments/ (binarytrees, fannkuch, fasta, knucleotide, mandelbrot, nbody, spectralnorm) compiled ahead of time to C with luaot and run through experiments/main.lua, versus the same scripts on the stock Lua 5.4.3 interpreter and LuaJIT; 20 runs each, wall-clock time.
corrections.caveats: CPU model and gcc version not stated (perf counters in statistics/perf-slow.txt only show about 3.06 GHz); the timing file is undated and comes from the paper's experiments. The paper itself (ACM DL, inf.puc-rio.br preprint) is blocked here, so its numbers are snippet only. Gains are uneven: 1.21x to 1.5x on four of seven benchmarks, about 2x to 2.6x only on fannkuch, mandelbrot and spectralnorm; LuaJIT is far faster on every benchmark. Based on Lua 5.4.3 (older than 5.4.7/5.5), every module must be compiled to C with a C compiler at build time, and the repo has had no commits since 2023-12-06.

notes: README quote verified and backed by raw timing data in statistics/times-slow.txt (LuaAOT 1.21x to 2.64x faster than Lua 5.4.3), plus a peer-reviewed SBLP 2021 paper whose abstract (snippet only) reports 20% to 60% lower running times; upgraded to B on that basis. If snippet-only paper evidence is not accepted, the repo data alone supports C. Licence MIT confirmed from LICENSE.txt (PUC-Rio plus Hugo Musso Gualandi); last commit 2023-12-06, stale. Shortcomings: no CPU/compiler version, uneven gains, far behind LuaJIT, old Lua 5.4.3 base, unmaintained since 2023.
